session.capture_method: Native Codex JSONL events plus timed copies; preload snapshots before CLI entry and 50ms polling for complete output JSON revisions. Transient unsubmitted drafts between polls are not guaranteed.
session.completeness: Native JSONL stream through process exit; tool output truncation, if any, remains visible; private reasoning is not requested.

observations.review_origin: Maintenance Codex review of final JSON, pinned source and saved full-page screenshot; author-side inspection, not human maintainer acceptance.
findings: Six components distinguish the browser, local PTY runtime, team protocol, CLI child processes and SQLite state. The browser's active xterm/WebSocket path is used; the unused sendWorkspaceUserInput helper is explicitly excluded from the primary UI path.

Delegation is an orchestrator decision, stdin delivery is separate from terminal output, and explicit report settlement is separate from output streaming. Progress messages are persisted without an orchestrator wake; optional status wakes without closing work. Report outbox delivery is acknowledged after a successful PTY write, not as proof of agent consumption.

Stopped-worker handling, CLI identity/roles and report seen-sequence checks match the source. The architecture omits detailed return arrows for SQL reads and HTTP polling but labels those relationships as reads/queries and explains returned results; it does not assert a separate transport or automatic completion.

First JSON passes validation. One voluntary simplification removes a redundant round-trip card while preserving nodes and all eleven relationships. One command exits with status 1 because a final rg query finds no update fields; this is not a generation or delivery failure.

The diagram and cards are readable. Several routes bend or cross in the center, but separation/halos keep them traceable; no observed node clipping or boundary-title masking. Secondary labels are small. All relationships remain forward, and fixed-input replay is identical across versions, so this run does not exercise the new direction fields.
observations.tool_count_definition: Completed shell command-execution items; compound shell subcommands are not counted independently. Native sessions retain their output and failures.

unavailable: Native client events do not isolate CLI runtime or provider queue/network waits; event arrival timestamps are retained without treating them as CPU time.
Pre-entry snapshots prove attempted candidate history. Polling also captures unvalidated drafts; transient complete unsubmitted drafts between 50 ms polls are not guaranteed.
No human maintainer or external independent acceptance is claimed.
